entry.title: Parliament Representation Reflects Diversity
entry.summary:
DHAKA, Bangladesh, November 23 (IPS) - Whether financial power is now winning the chance to represent people in Parliament, one of the fundamental questions with regard to the future of democracy in Bangladesh is: Do regular people, especially those with limited economic means, have a fair chance of accessing politics and their voice in national decision-making? Parliament should not become an exclusive club for the rich nor a financial institution where money outweighs political experience, public faith and patriotism to serve the public. A trusted democratic system of representation is threatened by the increasing role played by rich and influential people in electoral politics.

Read the full story, “Parliament Representation Reflects Diversity”, on globalissues.org →

entry.title: More Than a Cautionary Tale: Nepal’s Fight for Mountain Justice at COP31
entry.summary:
ANTALYA, Türkiye, November 23 (IPS) - At the UN climate conference (COP31) in Turkey, Nepal was part of almost every discussion around the climate crisis and climate-induced disasters. In the wake of the devastating flood in August, which the world witnessed through CCTV footage and whose impacts local communities are still living with, almost everyone at COP31 is talking about it as an example of a climate disaster.

entry.title: Security Council LIVE: Winter attacks on Ukraine's power grid and Black Sea shipping threaten lives and global food supplies
entry.summary:

It will also look at how strikes on Black Sea shipping threaten grain supplies to import-dependent countries far from the war’s frontline.
